correctness.rationale: The source proves that finite tuple meet-closures consist of pairwise meet terms and that the Rado meet-tree is the generic mix of finite graphs with finite meet-trees. A closure with \(n\) black generators and \(k\) additional meet points is exactly a rooted Greg tree. Generic mixing gives every simple graph on its \(n+k\) closure vertices, and tuple-fixing isomorphisms fix every meet term, so the factor \(2^{\binom{n+k}{2}}\) has no further quotient. Two exact computations of the Greg refinement agree with OEIS A048160 and with the displayed weighted totals.
